newsitem.title: USA: Boeing sees McDonnell deal accretive immediately.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sees McDonnell deal accretive immediately.

text.p: Boeing Co President and Chief Executive Officer Phil Condit said Monday he expects the merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp to be accretive to earnings immediately.
Condit, in a CNBC interview, said he expected to deal to be "accretive to earnings right out of the blocks."
He also said he would like to have the deal done in the next six months.
"We are positive the deal can be done in the next six months," including the clearance of anti-trust issues, Condit said.
Condit said there were no assurances from the U.S. Department of Defense related to anti-trust concerns before the merger was agreed on.
"Both of these companies are very much international and we are looking at this deal on a global scale," said Condit.
He added, "We are confident the Department of Defense reaction will be positive."
Both Condit and Harry Stonecipher, president and chief executive officer of McDonnell Douglas, said "the timing was right" for this deal.
"This is the deal we wanted and we are very happy with it...this is the only deal we considered," said Stonecipher.
He added, "We have been talking about this deal for two years."
